title: Text auf Bild
slide_intent: Adjust the image behind text so the message can be read without sacrificing the photograph’s role.
strategic_value: Selective tonal support can preserve DB imagery and clear communication together.
demonstration: Light and dark photo examples precede three comparison sliders for partial darkening, a dark gradient and a light gradient. The captured sliders expose part of each photographic scene and part of its tonal-support overlay artwork.
practical_value: Assess text contrast and consider local darkening or a subtle light/dark gradient behind the content.

content_islands.name: Initial comparison
content_islands.spec: Pair light and dark photographic examples below the introductory guidance.

content_islands.name: Partial darkening
content_islands.spec: Show the first labeled slider with white text and a white logo.

content_islands.name: Gradient options
content_islands.spec: Stack the dark-gradient and light-gradient comparison sliders with their explanations.

reference_purposes.Intent: The source frames adjustments as making text readable for all users.
reference_purposes.Application: It offers partial darkening and subtle light/dark gradient options.
reference_purposes.Constraint: The source cites WCAG 2.1 targets of at least 4.5:1 or 3:1 for large elements while also saying photographic contrast has no fixed measurement in the same way as graphics; retain that qualification.

ingredient.name: Tonal support behind text
ingredient.role: Improve text separation from photographic detail.
ingredient.application: Use local darkening or subtle dark/light gradients where needed.
ingredient.scope: Official DB new-design website captured 2026-11-05; edition date unstated. The source cites 4.5:1 or 3:1 for large elements; photographic evaluation is described as context-dependent.
